narrative: Demand for PL2__M1602110 exhibits high seasonal variability (CV=0.58) with a lognormal-like distribution and occasional zero-demand days. Lead times are stable (CV=0.28) but contribute the majority (57.8%) of lead-time demand variance due to demand magnitude. The EOQ of 14,272 units is capped to 10,655 by the storage capacity constraint, and the resulting policy achieves 95% service level at an annual cost of $5,748 versus $39,697 under the current SAP MOQ-only approach.
warnings: Capacity constraint binding: EOQ 14272 capped to 10655 (max_storage_units=14926.97, safety_stock=4271)
Two lead-time outliers detected at 13.61 and 13.64 days — potential supplier disruptions
Zero-demand days (~7%) present; policy uses robust standard deviation as cross-check
SAP safety lead time (5.0 days) exceeds recommended (3.49 days) — reduction advised

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is quasi-continuous with high daily volume and moderate intermittency, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy appropriate. The reorder point triggers replenishment when stock falls below expected lead-time demand plus safety stock, and the fixed order quantity (EOQ-derived, capacity-capped) balances ordering and holding costs efficiently.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is binding at 99.99% utilisation. The unconstrained EOQ would yield a lower total cost; the cap reduces order consolidation efficiency by ~34%, increasing annual ordering cost by approximately $590. Any safety stock increase beyond 4,271 units is infeasible without capacity expansion.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None. MOQ (772) + safety_stock (4271) = 5,043 < max_storage_units (14,927). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
